boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Gannon spaces for quiet work, group projects, creative production, fitness and between-class resets, with access cues grounded in university and student-media sources.

cards.entity_name: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.title: Match the Floor to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Quiet study, group rooms and open seating
cards.notes: Use the active lower levels for collaborative work, move to the silent third floor for focus, or reserve one of the library’s study rooms.
cards.short_summary: A library where each floor supports a different kind of work session.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s catalog describes Nash Library as containing quiet and collaborative spaces plus 49 study rooms for groups of two to ten students.
cards.source_title: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons | Gannon University Catalog
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations and some services are intended for Gannon students; consult the library website for current hours and access.

cards.title: Spread Out Between Meal Periods
cards.subtitle: A large shared work area near campus dining
cards.notes: Try the ballroom for a larger table-based work session, but plan around lunch and dinner when the university says space may be limited.
cards.short_summary: A roomy alternative when smaller study areas feel cramped.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s official study-space guide identifies Yehl Ballroom as a 48-seat study location and notes that space may be limited during lunch and dinner.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spaces on Campus
cards.access_notes: Availability can be limited during meal periods; confirm current building access before relying on the space.

cards.title: Choose Your Own Study Setup
cards.subtitle: Computer stations, lounges and reservable rooms
cards.notes: Start at a computer station for solo work, then move a group into a private or semi-private conference room when discussion becomes necessary.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus hub that can shift from solo concentration to group planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon states that Waldron Campus Center provides personal computer stations, quiet corners and reservable private or semi-private conference rooms for projects.
cards.access_notes: Conference rooms require reservations; building areas may follow campus schedules or event restrictions.

cards.title: Build a Work Session by Floor
cards.subtitle: Desks, café tables, computers and soft seating
cards.notes: Use the lower-level atrium for desk space, the café for table work or the upper-floor lounges when you need a smaller place to regroup.
cards.short_summary: A business building with several clearly different between-class work zones.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s study-space guide lists desks, café tables, computer stations and lounge seating throughout the Center for Business Ingenuity during class times.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spaces on Campus
cards.access_notes: The cited guide says listed areas are open during class times; verify current academic-building access.

cards.title: Claim a Lounge Seat Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Small work zones near engineering classrooms
cards.notes: Check the first-floor lounge near room 106 for tables, counter seats and soft seating; use the lobby when the lounge is occupied.
cards.short_summary: Compact seating options for short individual or small-group work blocks.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s official guide documents lobby seating, a first-floor lounge with tables and counter seats, desks and a lower-level conference table in the Center for Advanced Engineering.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spaces on Campus
cards.access_notes: The cited guide limits these areas to class times; classroom and conference-table availability may vary.

cards.title: Take the Group to Room 330
cards.subtitle: An 18-desk option in the science building
cards.notes: Head to the third-floor room when your group needs individual desk surfaces in one place, and finish before the listed building window closes.
cards.short_summary: A practical science-building setup for groups that need separate desks together.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s official study-space guide identifies third-floor room 330 in Zurn Science Center as an 18-desk study space.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spaces on Campus
cards.access_notes: The 2020 guide listed Zurn access from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; verify current hours and room availability.

cards.title: Find the Lounge That Fits the Group
cards.subtitle: Meeting rooms, lounges and outdoor tables
cards.notes: Check the Foreign Language Lounge for a larger group, use a smaller meeting room for focused conversation or take work outside to Peach Street.
cards.short_summary: Several specialized rooms make Palumbo useful for different group sizes.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s study-space guide lists multiple meeting rooms and lounges inside Palumbo Academic Center, plus outdoor tables along Peach Street.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spaces on Campus
cards.access_notes: Room availability depends on class and organizational use; check posted schedules before settling in.

cards.entity_name: Center for Communication and the Arts
cards.title: Work Where Student Media Gets Made
cards.subtitle: Radio, gallery, museum and production spaces
cards.notes: Pair a visit to the gallery or archaeology museum with a project session, while respecting that studios and instructional rooms may be restricted.
cards.short_summary: A creative academic building where exhibits and student-run media share an address.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon says the Center for Communication and the Arts houses learning spaces, student-run 90.5 WERG, an art gallery, an archaeology museum and a television film studio.
cards.source_title: Art in Every Corner | Gannon University
cards.access_notes: Academic studios and station facilities may be limited to enrolled students or supervised activities; follow posted access rules.

cards.title: Reset Without Leaving Campus
cards.subtitle: Pool, track, courts and fitness spaces
cards.notes: Choose the suspended track for steady movement, the courts for active time or a scheduled group class; bring your valid member ID for entry.
cards.short_summary: One building supports a quick movement break or a structured workout.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon documents an indoor field house, pool, basketball gym, suspended track, weight room, cardio deck, racquetball courts and daily group fitness classes at the center.
cards.access_notes: A valid member ID is required for member entry; guests need an eligible member sponsor and a purchased guest pass.

cards.title: Turn an Idea Into a Prototype
cards.subtitle: Collaborative innovation inside I-HACK
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from rapid prototyping, then ask staff about approved access to the 3D printers, laser scanners or soldering tools.
cards.short_summary: A shared innovation environment built around making, mapping and technical development.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon describes The Hatchery as a collaborative innovation space with 3D printers, laser scanners, soldering tools, geospatial mapping and supercomputing resources.
cards.source_title: Institute for Health and Cyber Knowledge | Gannon University
cards.access_notes: Equipment use may require authorization, instruction or affiliation with a course, project, internship or partner program.
